messages:
SRE-Bot: PAGER: P0 - inference-service 5xx spike across us-west-2. Error rate > 30% for last 3m. Paging oncall: @Maria L. Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/inference-p0 

Maria L.: On it. Jumping into the bridge now. Can someone drop quick impact numbers (request/sec, customers affected)? :eyes:

Alex C.: Observing 500s from runtime-gateway -> model-pool. 99th p95 latency also up. Quick query from ELK: `count(status:500) by 1m` shows ~3.2k/min at peak.

Julia P.: Noted. I pulled recent logs to s3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1909999999/ (contains runtime, gateway, and model kernel traces). Link: https://s3.console.aws/1909999999

Sam T.: Copy, downloading. Initial grep shows repeated errors: `kv-cache OOM` and `kernel mismatch` around the same window. Snippet: ```[runtime] 2026-03-12T18:02:11Z ERROR serve: failed to allocate kv cache: OOM``` Might be an autoscale failure + batch sizing problem.

Maria L.: Good find. Hypothesis A: KV cache saturation due to sudden seq length spike. Hypothesis B: GPU kernel mismatch after rolled kernel build (recent deploy 17:40 UTC). We need timeline. Who has deploy timeline?

Dave R.: I can confirm there was a runtime kernel rollout at 17:38 UTC to `runtime-4.2.1`. No canary flagged. Deploy link: https://deploys.redwood/internal/12345.

Emily K.: Traffic spike started ~17:55 UTC (clients with long sequences). I have per-customer breakdown: two customers account for ~48% of requests and their avg seq length jumped from 512->4096. Pasting top offenders: customer-a, customer-d.

Lena S.: Adding to timeline: 17:38 deploy -> 17:55 traffic change -> 18:01 first 5xx spike -> 18:05 paged. I'll start a concise timeline file in the docs bucket: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1909999999/timeline.md

Alex C.: Captured runtime heap, KV stats and kernel logs in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcd1234. Key metric: kv_cache_used went from 60% -> 100% in ~90s.

Maria L.: Operational goals: 1) mitigate customer impact now (reduce 5xx), 2) gather timeline & evidence for RCA, 3) prepare a brief status page update with impact/outage window. Who can prepare the status page draft?

Julia P.: I can draft the status page blurb. Proposed short draft: "We are investigating elevated error rates for inference requests in US-WEST-2 impacting a subset of inference workloads. Mitigations in progress; customers may see increased errors and latency. Next update in 30 minutes." I'll post to #statuspage-drafts after a review.

Sam T.: For mitigation, we can roll back kernel to 4.2.0 (known stable) OR enforce shorter max_seq for heavy customers via runtime config. Rollback will take ~6-8 minutes to scale and re-route; seq limit change is near-instant but may alter customer outputs. Which do we prefer?

Maria L.: Quick decision: Apply conservative seq cap for the two offending customers (customer-a, customer-d) + throttle batching for runtime to reduce kv pressure. Alex, can you push a beta config to block seq>1024 for those customers? Sam, prepare rollback plan if config change doesn't reduce errors in 10m.

Alex C.: Pushing config now: ```PUT /runtime/config
{ "customer_overrides": { "customer-a": {"max_seq":1024}, "customer-d": {"max_seq":1024} } }
``` Will monitor.

Ops Bot: Deploy config change complete. Route table updated for customer overrides.

(2m later) Alex C.: Early signal: 5xx rate dropped ~60% after overrides and reduced batch window. Request rate still high but errors trending down.

Maria L.: Great. Julia, proceed with status page draft and include mitigation steps and affected customers anonymized. Emily, can you quantify the number of unique users impacted and any SLOs breached?

Emily K.: On it. Preliminary: ~1.2k requests failed from 2 customers over 18:01-18:12 UTC. Estimated customer-visible errors ~0.7%. SLO breach for latency p95 for those customers. I'll produce numbers in 10m.

Lena S.: I'm assembling logs and a preliminary timeline in the doc: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1909999999/timeline.md — will add links to kernel logs and deploy artifacts.

Sam T.: Rollback standing by. If errors aren't below baseline by 18:25 UTC, I'll initiate rollback to runtime-4.2.0.

Maria L.: Assigning tasks: Julia (status page draft), Emily (impact numbers + customer list), Alex (monitor & iterate config), Sam (rollback ready), Lena (timeline + evidence), Dave (deploy artifact snapshot). I'll own comms to internal stakeholders after the next update.

(18:22 UTC) Maria L.: Update: Errors reduced to baseline. No rollback required. Continue with post-incident capture.

Julia P.: Posted statuspage draft to #statuspage-drafts: "[18:22 UTC] We mitigated elevated error rates affecting a subset of inference workloads in US-WEST-2. Customers with very long sequences experienced increased errors; we applied temporary customer caps and reduced batching which restored normal service. Engineers are continuing post-incident analysis"

Emily K.: Final impact numbers: 1,240 failed requests across 2 customers; potential revenue impact negligible; SLO hit noted for those customers between 17:58-18:12 UTC. CSV export of affected requests uploaded: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1909999999/impacted_requests.csv

Dave R.: I've archived deploy artifact and build logs here: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1909999999/deploy-artifact.tar.gz. No hotfix required.

Lena S.: Timeline doc updated with precise timestamps and log pointers. Will convert to RFC-style timeline for the RCA.

Maria L.: Next steps for RCA: - Owner: Lena (timeline + evidence) - Hypotheses: kv-cache pressure from seq spike vs kernel incompatibility — both documented - Data needed: per-request seq length distribution, kernel rollout metrics, batch window sizing history - Follow-up meeting: 09:00 UTC tomorrow with infra + runtime + eng-ml.

Alex C.: I'll open a follow-up ticket with checklist and link to this thread: RDW-INC-20260312-001.

Ops Bot: Incident resolved. Duration: 34 minutes. Notifying stakeholders channel.

Maria L.: Handoff: I'm handing oncall to @Lena S. in 10m. Please continue any outstanding postmortem tasks there. Thanks team — nice quick mitigation. :clap:
